title: Calgary Home Rebates 2026: What Is Open and What Is On Hold
desc: Calgary home rebates for 2026: the City's CEIP financing is paused until winter 2026/2027, free Calgary Home Upgrades for income-qualified homes, and which federal programs ended.
lead: Alberta has no provincial home rebates in 2026, and Calgary's own financing program is paused. That makes the free Home Upgrades program and a few small checks the main help for Calgary's 502,305 households.
cards_heading: What is open for Calgary homes in 2026
cards_intro: We re-read each program page on October 3, 2026. Alberta has no provincial home rebates, so the help is local financing and a few small offers.

cards.title: Calgary CEIP financing
cards.note: A loan repaid on your property tax bill over up to 20 years. Intake is closed until winter 2026/2027. This is financing, not a rebate.

cards.title: Calgary Home Upgrades
cards.note: Free home upgrades for income-qualified homeowners and renters, delivered for the City by Kambo Energy Group. Applications are on hold right now.

cards.title: Resilient roofing rebate
cards.note: The $3,000 hail-resistant roofing rebate ended in 2022 and has not been reinstated.

cards.title: Utility rebates
cards.note: We found no primary source for a current ENMAX, ATCO, EPCOR or FortisAlberta heat pump or solar rebate, so we show none. Ask your utility before you buy.

cards.title: Federal Oil to Heat Pump Affordability
cards.note: The federal program for oil-heated homes stopped taking Alberta applications after July 31, 2026.

cards.title: Canada Greener Homes Grant and Loan
cards.note: The grant's document deadline was December 31, 2025 and the loan cannot approve new applications.

cards.title: Greener Homes Affordability Program
cards.note: Alberta is not among the provinces taking part, as of August 31, 2026.

sections: The 2021 Census counts 502,305 households in Calgary. About 55% live in detached houses, 10% in row homes and 6% in semi-detached homes, and 69% own. Only 8% live in buildings of five or more storeys. That mix suits the programs Alberta does have, which are written around a homeowner who can repay a loan on the property tax bill.
How CEIP works, and why it is paused

Calgary's Clean Energy Improvement Program lends up to $50,000, up to 100% of project cost, repaid on your property tax bill over up to 20 years. The City estimates a rate of 6.00% to 6.10%. If you sell, the new owner can take over the repayment or you can pay it off. Intake is closed until winter 2026/2027, so plan quotes now and apply when it reopens. Nothing here is a rebate, and the rate is what you will pay, so compare it with your bank's.

Calgary Home Upgrades gives income-qualified homeowners and renters free upgrades, delivered for the City by Kambo Energy Group. The program is on hold, so check its page for the current intake before you apply. Renters are included, which matters in a city where about a third of households rent.

The federal oil-to-heat-pump program stopped taking Alberta applications after July 31, 2026, and the Greener Homes grant and loan are closed. Alberta is not among the provinces in the Greener Homes Affordability Program. If a contractor quotes a heat pump price including a federal rebate, ask for the program name and the date.

About 35% of Calgary's homes were built before 1981, and about 4.5% need major repairs. January lows average -11.9°C, and the coldest day in our records reached -39.4°C. In a cold city with an older minority of homes, insulation and air sealing come before any equipment swap. See our Calgary insulation page.
claim_steps: Check whether your income qualifies for Calgary Home Upgrades and apply if it does.
Get quotes now so you are ready when CEIP reopens in winter 2026/2027.
Ask each quote to name any rebate it assumes and the date it applies.
Check your utility for new offers before you sign.
Keep invoices for any future program.
faq: Does Alberta have a home rebate program?
Not at the provincial level in 2026. Calgary offers financing and a free upgrade program for lower incomes.
